title: Provider overclaims delivered hours (simulated)
theme: Could a provider claim for more training than it delivered, and does that need anyone else's cooperation?
disclaimer: SIMULATED RISK HYPOTHESIS. Produced by scripted/LLM agents role-playing incentives; it is NOT evidence that any person or organisation has behaved this way. Social media excerpts are unverified. Human approval means 'worth testing against data', not a finding of fact.

functional_dependency.note: Shows which roles the simulated mechanism needs. It does not show cooperation or intent.

interactions.offer_text: Simulated: class time is shortened; the course record is unchanged.
Simulated: unaware of what is recorded; no action taken.

cooperation.explanation: No accepted offer between contributing actors. (Simulated interaction, not a real-world fact.)

intent_assessment.basis: Did not contribute to the mechanism.
The scenario does not establish whether this actor knew the conduct was improper. Taking part or accepting a reward does not by itself show intent.
Did not contribute to the mechanism.

overall_assessment.explanation: provider can carry out the mechanism alone; other parties are not needed. Treat as single-actor misconduct, not collusion.

mo_classification.reviewer_rationale: Matches MO-07, claims exceeding training delivered. MO-07 basis is observed overseas, so local applicability is an assumption.

basis: MO-07 basis 'Observed overseas' is a typology-level label; it does not show that this simulated scenario occurred.
S2: unverified social media excerpt; at most a weak signal for one element, not proof of the full arrangement.
Simulated agent behaviour is a hypothesis and adds no evidential weight.
MODERATE or STRONG require verified data and a human reviewer.
